source_text: Nescio sane, utrum hic iam coactus inopia, tam ineptum, tam imbecillum aliquid moliaris, ut dicas, nullis te quidem rationibus docere posse Adam bonum a Deo conditum, sed ad hoc credendum sola esse lectionis auctoritate contentum, qua post formatum hominem sexto iam die communiter de omnibus creaturis refertur: Et vidit Deus omnia quae fecit, et ecce bona valde [n80] . Quod non pro opificis dignitate, non pro appensione eius iustitiae, sed pro testimonio, quo communiter quae creata sunt, bene facta dicuntur, Adam quoque haud iniquum aestimes institutum. Porro licet hoc Manichaeum tam leviter pulset, ut rideat; Traducianum tamen revinctum exponit nobis. Ut enim nullo testimoniorum divinorum in hanc rem populos congregemus; Apostoli solius auctoritate praescribimus, qui cum foedum praevideret errorem, celso adversum vos ore detonuit dicens: Quoniam omnis creatura Dei bona est [n81] . Si ergo ad probandum bonae naturae primum hominem fuisse formatum, sufficit hoc quod dicit Moyses, universa Deum bene condidisse, perque hoc tu cum peccato creari a Deo Adam non potuisse contendis, quia bonus inter reliqua legitur institutus; iisdem lineis referemus, per hoc nullum posse cum peccato nasci, quoniam ab Apostolo omnis creatura Dei bona esse defenditur. Quid ergo his disputationibus actum est? Videlicet, ut id quod ratio indagarat, optio quoque indicti inter te et Manichaeum praelii publicaret; ut cum proposito certamine ne unum quidem telum sine tua pernicie in praeceptorem tuum vibrare posses, multo manifestissime reluceret, vos et Manichaeos in unum impietatis corpus obscena coaluisse concordia. Quid enim potest esse tam iunctum, quam quod nec discriminum separatur incursu? Omni exitio Manichaei, Traducianorum dogma commoritur; nihil est quod illum feriat, et te relinquat. Una vobis sunt instituta, una mysteria, unaque pericula; et substomacharis, si senis Manis soboles nuncupere?
pass_a_gloss: I do not know indeed whether here already compelled by poverty you will try something so inept, so weak, that you say you can indeed teach by no reasons that Adam was founded good by God, but are content for believing this by the authority of the reading alone, by which after the human was formed on the sixth day already it is commonly reported about all creatures: And God saw all things which he made, and behold they were very good. Which not for the craftsman's dignity, not for a weighing of his justice, but for a testimony by which commonly those things which were created are said well made, you would estimate Adam also instituted not unjust. Further although this so lightly strikes Manichaeus that he laughs; nevertheless it exposes the Traducian bound to us. For that we may gather the peoples by no testimonies of divine things into this matter; we prescribe by the authority of the Apostle alone, who when he foresaw a foul error, thundered with a lofty mouth against you saying: Because every creature of God is good. If therefore for proving that the first human was formed of a good nature, this suffices which Moses says, that God founded all things well, and through this you contend that Adam could not have been created by God with sin, because he is read instituted good among the rest; by the same lines we will report that through this no one can be born with sin, because by the Apostle every creature of God is defended as good. What therefore has been done by these disputations? Namely that what reason had tracked, the choice also of a battle declared between you and Manichaeus would publish; so that when a contest having been proposed you could not even vibrate one weapon without your destruction against your teacher, it would shine much most manifestly that you and the Manichaeans had coalesced by an obscene concord into one body of impiety. For what can be so joined, as what is not even separated by an onset of discriminations? By every destruction of Manichaeus, the dogma of the Traducians dies with him; there is nothing which would strike him and leave you. You have one institutions, one mysteries, and one dangers; and you are angry if you are named offspring of old Manes?

pass_b_english: I do not know whether, now driven by lack of resources, you might attempt something so foolish and weak as saying you cannot prove by any reasons that God created Adam good, but are satisfied to believe it solely on the authority of the reading. After humanity was formed on the sixth day, it says of all creatures together: ‘God saw everything he had made, and behold, it was very good’ (Genesis 1:31). You would thus judge Adam to have been established without injustice, not because of the maker’s dignity or a weighing of his justice, but because of the testimony calling all created things well made.

Yet although this strikes Mani so lightly that he laughs, it exposes the advocate of inherited sin bound before us. We need gather no crowd of divine testimonies here. The apostle’s authority alone supplies our ruling: foreseeing this foul error, he thundered against you in lofty speech, ‘Every creature of God is good’ (1 Timothy 4:4).

If Moses’ statement that God made everything well suffices to prove the first human was formed with a good nature, and you therefore insist Adam could not have been created by God with sin because he is read to have been made good among the rest, we will answer along exactly the same lines: no one can be born with sin, because the apostle defends every creature of God as good.

What have these arguments accomplished? The choice offered you in the contest declared between you and Mani has publicly revealed what reason discovered. Once the contest was proposed, you could not hurl even one weapon at your teacher without destroying yourself. Thus it shines still more clearly that you and the Manichaeans have fused through obscene agreement into a single body of impiety. What could be more closely joined than what not even the arrival of danger can separate? In every destruction of Mani, the doctrine of inherited sin dies with him. Nothing strikes him and leaves you intact. Your principles, mysteries, and dangers are one—and you resent being called old Mani’s offspring?

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
